filename: Attention‐Based Stochastic Simulation of Climate‐Informed Spatiotemporal Flood Risk for Multisite Insurance Portfolios.pdf
title: Attention‐Based Stochastic Simulation of Climate‐Informed Spatiotemporal Flood Risk for Multisite Insurance Portfolios
testbed_rationale: The datasets and methods focus on streamflow time-series modeling, climate teleconnections, and stochastic flood simulation for portfolio risk rather than physical parameterization of Earth system processes or high-resolution GCM emulator testbeds.
pain_points: Data limitation: extreme value and heavy-tailed hydroclimate risk distributions require long records; pure deep learning architectures tend to overfit and fail on out-of-sample extremes without long historical observations.
Curse of dimensionality in nonparametric analog/kNN methods when scaling to multisite portfolios.
Mismatch between subdecadal/interannual fiscal decision horizons (1-5 years) and traditional seasonal forecast (months) or GCM projection (multidecadal/centennial) scales.
extraction_notes: The paper uses a hybrid approach combining a Transformer encoder to create low-dimensional climate state embeddings, coupled with kNN analog retrieval and empirical copulas to sample daily streamflow flood sequences.
